title: Petra and the Static
premise: Beatrix Thornbury has spent eleven years alone tending Petra, Earth's last seed vault, running supply routes between colonies that severed contact after the Silence. When the colony's children begin dreaming the same dream — a voice counting down from a relay at the edge of dead space — Beatrix realizes the old network isn't dead; it's waking, and something inside it is calling the children home. With a stowaway girl named Ilex who claims the dream chose her, Beatrix races to the relay to answer or silence it. At the relay she discovers the signal is a compressed archive of every mind lost when the network collapsed, and answering it means feeding it living memories to rebuild itself. Beatrix sacrifices her own memories of the vault — her whole life's meaning — to free the children and let the archive finally rest, returning home remembering nothing but a feeling of having been loved.
about_author: Vesper Sterling is the pen name of a former radio technician who spent a decade maintaining remote transmitter stations in the far north before turning to fiction. Their work explores loneliness at planetary scale and the stubborn machinery of hope.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She runs her annual supply circuit between silent colonies, logging dead relays and talking to herself to stay sane. Establishes her ritual care of the seed vault and her refusal to grieve the lost network. Emotional beat: competent solitude curdling into loneliness she won't name.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Dream
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Ilex, twelve, on colony Meridian, where every child wakes at 3:11 a.m. having dreamed of a corridor of light and a voice counting down. The adults call it a fever; the children start leaving each other notes in a language none of them learned. Beat: eerie wonder and the first crack in the world's quiet.

chapters.title: Stowaway
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Mid-route, she finds Ilex hiding in a seed crate, clutching a hand-drawn map of a relay Beatrix thought was scrap. Ilex insists the dream gave it to her. Beatrix plans to turn back; the nav system refuses — someone has locked in new coordinates. Beat: reluctant responsibility, first spark of found family.

chapters.title: What the Vault Keeps
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV aboard ship. She interviews Beatrix about the old network for her 'dream journal,' and Beatrix accidentally reveals she helped build the relay that's now calling. Ilex realizes the dream knows things only Beatrix could know. Beat: trust deepening alongside dread.

chapters.title: Dead Space Radio
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. They pass the boundary where all signals die, and the countdown from the dream begins playing over the ship's speakers — audible without power. Beatrix admits the collapse eleven years ago wasn't an accident; she signed the shutdown order that stranded the minds inside. Beat: guilt surfaces; the race becomes personal penance.

chapters.title: The Colony That Answered
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. They dock at a colony gone strangely serene: adults sleepwalk through days while children gather nightly to sing the countdown in unison. A child tells Ilex the voice says it only needs one more memory to finish waking. Beat: horror wearing a gentle face; stakes made flesh.

chapters.title: Relay Nine
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Arrival at the relay: a cathedral of dead servers humming with borrowed dreams. Inside, the archive manifests as voices of everyone lost in the collapse — including Beatrix's sister, who died because of her order. It offers a bargain: give it living memory, and it will spare the children. Beat: temptation and grief entwined.

chapters.title: Counting Down
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The countdown hits its final hours; children across the colonies begin walking toward their local uplinks in their sleep. Ilex, half-caught in the dream herself, begs Beatrix to just say yes and end it. Beatrix nearly does. Beat: lowest point — love almost surrendering to guilt.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, climax. Instead of feeding it fragments, Beatrix offers the whole archive of herself — every memory of the vault, the routes, the years — arguing that survival bought by harvesting children is no survival at all. The archive accepts, and as it fills with her life it remembers how to end rather than persist. Beat: sacrifice as answer, not defeat.

chapters.title: Seeds
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV, resolution. The relays go quiet; the children wake remembering the dream fondly, like a lullaby. Ilex brings Beatrix — memoryless but alive — back to Petra, where the seeds are blooming out of season. Beatrix doesn't know why she cries at the sight. Ilex takes her hand: 'You kept us. Now I'll keep you.' Beat: grief transmuted into found family.
